abstract.text: Move a project from FirebladeECS 1.x to 2.0: components become value types, and every write goes through the nexus.

inlineContent.text: In FirebladeECS 2 components are value types. You write them as structs, reading one returns a copy, and every write goes through
closure. Entity identifiers carry a generation, so a destroyed entity never matches a later one. The state machine and the macros are separate products.

Most projects migrate in three moves: fix the 1.x deprecation warnings, turn component classes into structs, and replace the writes that relied on reference semantics. One of those writes is invisible to the compiler: read
Work in this order. Every step builds on its own, so you can commit after each one.
